test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 28 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about Nilgiri Hills?

options.text: It is located in Western Ghats of India.
It is a mountainous region of Karnataka.
Doddabetta is the highest peak of these hills.
Tea and Coffee are grown extensively on these hills.

solution:
The correct answer is I**__t is a mountainous region of karnataka.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Nilgiri Hills**

 
 
• Southern India's **Nilgiri Hills** is a region of **mountains, forests, and tea and coffee plantations** that is shared by the states of **Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka**.
 
• The** purple-blue Neelakurunji flowers **that grow in the **Shola forests** of the Nilgiri hills are the origin of the name for these mountains.
 
• They join the **Western and Eastern Ghats at the trijuction** of the three states of Karnataka, Kerela, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is the part of the **Western Ghats** of India.
 
• There are at least **24 peaks** in the Nilgiri Mountains that are higher than** 2,000 metres (6,600 feet)**, with** Doddabetta being the highest peak at 2,637 metres (8,652 ft)**.
 
• It is not the mountainous region of Karnataka, it is the** mountainous region of Tamil Nadu**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Several odd tribal groups, including the **Toda, Kota, Badaga, and Kurumba**, are found in the Nilgiri Hills. 
 
• The Nilgiri Hills are a **protected bio-reserve in India and are a part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve**, which is a part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
 
• The **Moyar River** separates the Nilgiri Hills from the **Karnataka Plateau to the north**. 
 
• **Kolakambai Fall**, the **highest waterfall**, is located north of Kolakambai Hill and drops 400 feet without interruption (120 m).
 
• With the **second-highest annual rainfall in India**, the Nilgiri Hills receive almost **14 feet of rain annually**.
